short: A heavily armed American four-engine heavy bomber that formed the core of the daylight strategic bombing campaign over Europe.
full:
The Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress entered service in 1938 as a fast, high-flying strategic bomber. It was defined by its extensive defensive armament, carrying up to thirteen heavy machine guns to fend off enemy interceptors. Deployed extensively by the United States Army Air Forces in Europe, the B-17 was the primary instrument of the American daylight precision bombing campaign against German industrial and military targets, while the Royal Air Force bombed by night.

Operating in massive, tight formations to maximize their overlapping fields of fire, B-17 crews suffered appalling casualties during unescorted missions over Germany before long-range fighters like the P-51 Mustang became available. Despite the losses, the aircraft earned a legendary reputation for its ability to absorb catastrophic battle damage and still return its crew safely. Over twelve thousand were built, dropping hundreds of thousands of tons of bombs before the war's end.
